pairs.note: Canonical pair: deployment information is exactly matched; training and compute costs differ and are transparently recorded.
One baseline receives fewer sensors than the paired reference; this is not an information-equivalent trial.
One baseline receives twice the sampling rate.
Baselines are evaluated under different disturbance realizations.
One baseline is scored against a weaker service-floor profile.
One baseline receives more permissive actuator authority.
One baseline is scored over half the observation horizon.
A baseline attempts to access future covariates unavailable to its paired comparator.
A single baseline cannot constitute a paired comparison.
A baseline without an exact configuration digest cannot produce a reproducible comparative result.

interpretation_rules: Every baseline in a pair must receive a deployment_inputs object exactly equal to the pair's shared_deployment_inputs object.

Deployment input parity covers scenario, network, topology, geometry, demand and disturbance traces, random seed, sensor set, sampling, missingness, time grid, units, scoring horizon, service-floor profile, required area set, actuator envelope, local protection contract, decision deadline and no-future-covariate declaration.
Development resource budgets may differ across baselines but each component must be explicitly recorded; no missing training/compute/engineer-hour fields are permitted.
A baseline cannot use future covariates unavailable to the paired comparator.
Every baseline requires version, configuration digest, implementation artifact, execution environment, runtime version, data population and split receipt.
Leak dataset split admission is owned by #5053/#4979; this matched-trial evaluator only requires the exact split receipt reference and does not replace split-integrity checks.
Abstention and eligible coverage must be scored alongside risk or accuracy; abstained cases cannot be silently dropped.
All scorecards retain service, event, uncertainty, resilience, resource and evidence-integrity dimensions separately; no single compensatory score is authoritative.
A failed pair is rejected from comparative scoring but retained in the receipt with the specific mismatch reason.
Synthetic input digests and budgets are design placeholders, not measured data, vendor performance, procurement prices or operating conditions.
claim_ceiling: Synthetic paired-input admission semantics only. No algorithm or commercial platform performance is measured or ranked.
